learningObjective: Distinguish claims about FlashAttention that are algorithm-level truths from common overgeneralizations about performance.

canonicalClaims.claim: FlashAttention (v1/v2) is an exact attention algorithm with unchanged forward FLOPs and HBM I/O of O(N^2 d / M) where M is on-chip memory per SM; backward recomputes softmax probabilities block-by-block from stored (m, l) row statistics, trading FLOPs for I/O.
conditions: Standard attention with causal or non-causal mask.
nonImplications: Does not imply universal wall-clock speedup independent of shape/hardware.
Does not imply FLOP count is reduced.

misconceptions.claim: FlashAttention gives a fixed 3-4x speedup on all hardware and shapes.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Speedup varies significantly with N, d, batch, and hardware.
It is exact up to summation-order rounding.
Forward FLOPs unchanged; I/O is what's reduced.

implementationFacts: FA v2 improves parallelism over v1 by splitting work along the seq dim.
FA has been generalized to Hopper (FA3) with async copy and warp-specialization.
performanceScenarios: Speedup is largest on long sequences and small batches; benefit shrinks for very small N.
Backward speedup relative to naive is larger than forward because of quadratic P memory saved.
